title: From force diagrams to motion
target: Use a force diagram to predict acceleration and velocity change.
criteria: Write a force sum along each chosen axis.
Connect net force and mass to acceleration.
Use velocity direction to decide the initial speed change.

authoring.limitations: Reasoning evidence only. Multiple choice does not certify physical performance. Teacher reviews before assigning and rates mastery separately.

cpa.prompt: Take right and up as positive. Forces are 17 N right, 5 N left, 22 N up, and 22 N down. What are net components?
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A block slides down a ramp. Gravity’s along-ramp component is 18 N down and friction is 6 N up. With down-ramp positive, what is the force sum?
cpa.guide: Opposing forces need opposite signs on the chosen axis.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A 4 kg block has net force 12 N down a ramp. What is along-ramp acceleration?
options: 0 m/s² because it is on a ramp.
cpa.guide: a = F_net/m = 12/4 = 3 along the net force.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A 2.5 kg cart has net components Fx = −10 N and Fy = 0. What are acceleration components?
cpa.guide: Divide each force component by 2.5 kg.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A cart’s velocity is 5 m/s left and acceleration is 2 m/s² left. What is the initial speed change?
cpa.guide: Acceleration and velocity point the same way.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: A cart moves right with a constant leftward net force. Which sequence is possible if the force continues long enough?
options: It keeps the same rightward velocity forever.
It slows, stops momentarily, then speeds up left.
It loses mass until force vanishes.
cpa.guide: Leftward acceleration first reduces positive velocity, then makes it negative.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Compare evidence and identify a physical relationship.
